properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: hash.js@1.1.7 (yarn.lock, transitive via elliptic and friends) implements the SHA family including SHA-1. No direct first-party call site; the package ships the algorithms to the tree. If SHA-1 use matters, the fix is upgrading the transitive consumer, not this repo's code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 in this repo exists only in e2e tooling as file-content hashes for test selection (llmTestSelector, selectTestsByChangedFiles) — non-security purpose, both sites confirmed; kept as weak-hash posture data.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 in this repo: one live call in the icons build script (cache-key hash) and the sha1 crate shipped in the Rust bluetooth transport (tungstenite WS accept-key; lockfile also carries chacha20/rand CSPRNG). Both sites confirmed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is the signing curve for every Bitcoin-family network this wallet supports: coins.json declares it per coin (including the secp256k1_groestl variant), and noble-compatibility.ts adapts @noble/curves secp256k1 for utxo-lib transaction signing. Quantum-vulnerable (Shor), but the curve is dictated by each blockchain protocol — observable here, replaceable only by the networks themselves, not by this repo.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (Node.js 24)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All ten Node HTTPS/TLS session sites are real default-settings sessions on Node 24 (no PQ group configured): auth-server OAuth token exchange (carries client_secret/refresh tokens), blockchain-link-utils token metadata fetches, connect-explorer changelog/npm fetches, e2e mock proxy, and interceptor test plumbing. Classical X25519 key exchange only — harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to the OAuth and metadata traffic. Migrate to X25519MLKEM768 hybrid once Node enables it by default.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge@1.4.0 is resolved in yarn.lock and ships an RSA implementation (plus a JS TLS stack). No first-party call site found in this repo — the dependency makes the algorithms available to anything that imports it. Transitive; changeable here by pruning/upgrading the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves dependency of packages/device-authenticity; the secp256k1 module ships with the package (available in the shipped library; the package's own signature verification is ed25519/P-256 per its code). Dependency inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key agreement is the THP (Trezor Host Protocol) Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 pairing handshake — 9 production sites confirmed (pairing DH points, keypair factory, masked-static-pubkey check, public export) plus one live unit-test op; 4 test-scaffold/title sites rejected. Quantum-vulnerable custom-protocol key agreement outside TLS; migrate to ML-KEM-768 hybrid (the ML-KEM module already ships via @noble/post-quantum).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256/ECDSA (prime256v1) in this codebase: production use is device-authenticity signature verification (verifySignatures.ts, WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 params) and the same curve in firmware-release JWT (ES256) and trading payment-request validation exercised by these tests. Classical curve — Shor-vulnerable; production verification sites are the migration concern (ML-DSA), tests only exercise them.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA in this repo: production device-authenticity verification (verifySignatures.ts:36, WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 — quantum-vulnerable, migrate to the ML-DSA-44 path already shipped alongside it) plus ECDSA implementations in the dependency tree (yarn.lock). Two prose/scaffold sites rejected.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves (providing Ed25519) is a production dependency of device-authenticity; the production verifier calls ed25519.verify in verifySignatures.ts (algorithm-usage sites are tracked under the Ed25519 object ALG-5e08bdf5). Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable; ML-DSA-44 path already exists alongside it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 module available via @noble/curves in device-authenticity; the production P-256 verification in this package actually goes through WebCrypto SubtleCrypto (tracked under ALG-92e838c9). Dependency-availability entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.6.1 (classic JS EC library providing ECDH/ECDSA over secp256k1 and friends) is locked in the dependency tree — shipped with the build; no first-party call site resolved in this scan. Quantum-vulnerable ECDH capability present in the shipped dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Post-quantum ML-DSA (MLDSA44, FIPS 204) verification path in packages/device-authenticity — the PQ migration for device authenticity, live alongside the legacy ECDSA/Ed25519 path: production verifySignatureMLDSA44 calls ml_dsa44.verify (from @noble/post-quantum), X.509 cert parsing maps OID 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.17 to MLDSA44, production config carries rootPubKeysMLDSA root trust anchors per device model (T3W1 etc.), algorithm dispatch on 'MLDSA44', and mocks/fixtures/e2e tests carry the same con

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM is the authenticated-encryption layer of the THP Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 channel (aesgcm.ts wrapper consumed by pairing.ts, encode.ts, decode.ts — IVs from session nonce counters; the pairing.ts:41 zero-IV use is the standard Noise handshake-message convention under an ephemeral per-message key), plus AES-256-GCM for Suite metadata (metadataUtils.ts, random IV) and suite-native platform encryption (nativePlatformEncryption.ts, random IV), and the AES-GCM implementation shipped in de

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 in live use: THP protocol hashing (pairing secrets, hash combining in tools.ts), trading API request signing and API-key digest, native mobile platform-encryption key hashing (mmkv key derivation), coinjoin account-key hashing, payment-request output hashing, plus build/test hashing (Cardano CSL asmjs inputs, LLM test analyzer, Expo env config). Strong hash; Grover square-root only. Keep.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE2b/BLAKE2s in three live uses: Zcash zip-244 transaction digest components (blake2b with personalization in utxo-lib), address validation in the bitcoin-family validator, and a keyed blake2s MAC computing the Trezor firmware hash checked against the device. Quantum-resistant enough for hashing (Grover square-root only); no migration action needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256/512 across the repo's key-derivation surfaces: the Trezor Host Protocol (THP) chaining-key derivation (Signal-style tempKey/output1/output2 chain in tools.ts, hashed secrets in pairing.ts), Tor control-port SAFECOOKIE client auth, BIP32 HD-wallet derivation (hmacSHA512 over chain code / 'Bitcoin seed'), and Suite metadata key derivation (master key HMAC, HMAC-SHA-512 metadata key, passwords filename MAC). MACs keyed from secrets — Grover square-root applies to HMAC, no urgent migrat

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's pre-standard SHA-3 variant, via @noble/hashes keccak_256) in live use: EIP-55 address checksum validation, smart-chain address validation (keccak256 and blake256+keccak256 cases), and Monero key-image-sync protocol hashing (Monero's crypto is Keccak-based). Also exercised in unit tests and an e2e trading mock. Hashing only — Grover square-root applies; no urgent migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Noise-style HKDF (RFC 5869, HMAC-SHA-256 extract/expand implemented in protocol-thp/crypto/tools.ts) driving the THP pairing key schedule: hkdf1–hkdf4 derive chaining keys and temp keys from the X25519 DH points and the Noise_XX protocol name. Symmetric KDF itself is PQ-robust, but the secrets it derives come from the quantum-vulnerable X25519 agreement.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (WebCrypto subtle.deriveBits) in connect-core's firmware entropy verification — implements the SLIP-39 Shamir-mnemonic round function: 4 rounds × floor((10000 << 1)/4) = 5000 iterations each, 20000 total, salt = salt‖r with empty passphrase, per the SLIP-39 spec (interoperability fixes the count; OWASP's 600k guidance does not apply to spec-bound formats). Also the pbkdf2 npm package in the dependency tree (yarn.lock).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.4.0 ships AES (and a full X.509/PKI stack) in the dependency tree; no first-party call site resolved — capability present in the shipped build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) is available in the shipped @noble/post-quantum@0.6.1 module set of device-authenticity, but a workspace-wide grep finds no slh_dsa call site in application code — available in the shipped library, not yet used. Candidate alternative to ML-DSA-44 for device authenticity.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes SHA-256 module declared by network-bitcoin-suite-common (package.json) — the hash provider behind the Bitcoin-family address validation and hashing in that package. Presence is the finding; the use sites are judged under the SHA-256 and BLAKE objects.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes BLAKE3 module declared by network-bitcoin-suite-common (package.json) — provider for BLAKE3 hashing in the Bitcoin-family suite-common package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) is available in the shipped @noble/post-quantum@0.6.1 module set, but no ml_kem call site exists in application code — the THP channel still does classical X25519 key agreement. The PQ KEM needed for the X25519→ML-KEM-768 migration is already on disk, unused.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: @noble/hashes SHA-3/Keccak module declared by network-bitcoin-suite-common (package.json) — provider for the keccak_256 address-checksum validation confirmed under the SHA-3 object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 (createHash('sha512')) in THP pairing — hashing during the pairing handshake (device static-key verification material); meets CNSA 2.0 digest sizes. Quantum impact on hashes is only Grover's square-root speedup.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-GCM in three production surfaces: (1) THP host-device channel (aesgcm.ts createCipheriv/createDecipheriv 'aes-256-gcm', encode/decode with counter-derived IVs), (2) Suite desktop metadata encryption (metadataUtils.ts CIPHER_TYPE, random IV), (3) suite-native platform storage encryption (nativePlatformEncryption.ts, random IV). AES-256 retains 128-bit security margin under Grover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ciphers@1.3.0 locked in yarn ships ChaCha20-Poly1305 (and AES) — capability present in the shipped build; checking for call sites is part of my widening pass. ChaCha20-Poly1305 retains a 128-bit margin under Grover (256-bit keys).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CSPRNG (node crypto.randomBytes) at five production sites: device-authenticity challenge generation, Tor control-port SAFECOOKIE client nonce, AES-GCM IV generation for native platform encryption and for Suite metadata encryption, and MCP-server auth token generation. This is the good path — it also corroborates that the rejected 'static IV' object had no production basis.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Credential surface of the repo: three empty .example.env templates documenting CI credential names (Currents API key, LLM passphrase, GitHub tokens — no material committed) and the Android debug-keystore credentials.json with the universal public debug defaults ('android'); all four sites confirmed as credential-surface declarations.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/post-quantum ^0.6.1 is linked as a production dependency of @trezor/device-authenticity (and tracked in the public-package-dependencies requirements snapshot for connect) — provides ML-DSA (FIPS 204; used in production device-authenticity verification), ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) modules. The PQ capability of this repo lives here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Post-quantum crypto library: @noble/post-quantum is declared at the root and in packages/device-authenticity — it provides the ML-DSA (and ML-KEM) implementations behind the device-authenticity package's PQ verification path for newer devices. This is the migration target for the classical Ed25519/P-256 authenticity signatures; its presence shows the PQ migration path already exists in-house. Changeable here (version upgrades).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is the hash provider across the network packages (17 files: keccak/SHA-3 for Ethereum address validation, SHA-256/ripemd for Ripple/Stellar/Tron/Bitcoin validators, HMAC-SHA-256 in connect-core verifyEntropy.ts, BLAKE in address validators). Central dependency for all first-party hashing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is the EC provider across 5 declaration/usage points: device-authenticity (ed25519.verify production), utxo-lib (secp256k1 via noble-compatibility layer for BIP32), and suite-common/delegated-identity-key (getProofOfDelegatedIdentity.ts — delegated identity proofs). Ships secp256k1/P-256/ed25519 with the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 certificate handling available two ways: node-forge@1.4.0 in the dependency tree, and the project's own production X.509/ASN.1 parser in device-authenticity (x509certificate.ts) that reads device-authenticity certificates and maps signature-algorithm OIDs (e.g. 2.16.840.1.101.3.4.3.17 → MLDSA44). The PKI object class for device-authenticity certs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the `jose` package (yarn.lock) implements JOSE — JWS/JWE/JWK — for the tree. JWS verification utilities in suite-common/suite-utils (verifyJws) are the first-party consumers of JOSE-formatted objects; the ES256 signing/JWS sites are judged under the JWT ES256 object. Same logical asset as LIB-7ab7aaf6 (the package).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jws@4.0.1 is a declared dependency of connect-core: JWS (JSON Web Signature) processing for the signed firmware-release configuration — the production verifier in firmwareReleaseConfigUtils.ts validates ES256-signed release configs (algorithm use tracked under ALG-36874020 JWT ES256). JOSE/JWS is a protocol-configuration surface where the signing algorithm travels in the token header.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the `openpgp` package declared by suite/desktop-app-main (package.json) implements the OpenPGP protocol — the desktop app's PGP encryption/signing support (Trezor devices can host GPG keys). OpenPGP's classical algorithms (RSA/EdDSA/ElGamal) are quantum-vulnerable; capability is vendor+protocol dictated (OpenPGP card standard on the device), app-side algorithm choice is limited to what OpenPGP.js and the device firmware support. Same logical asset as LIB-50c426aa.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the `jwa` package (yarn.lock) implements JWA — the JSON Web Algorithms (HS256/RS256/ES256 signing and verification). Transitive (jsonwebtoken-style stacks); its ES256 path is what JWT/JWS verification in this repo exercises. Same logical asset as LIB-6ee6570a.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: openpgp (OpenPGP.js) is declared by suite/desktop-app-main — the concrete package implementing the OpenPGP asset recorded as ALG-681ce0cd. Ships classical public-key crypto (RSA, EdDSA, ElGamal); no direct call site judged here, presence is the finding.
